{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Reese T. Prosser 1974 (portion A).jpg|thumb|Prosser in 1974]]
'''Reese Trego Prosser''' (May 18, 1927 in [[Minneapolis]] &ndash; June 15, 1996) was an American mathematician.

He studied at [[Harvard University]] (A.B., 1949) and [[University of California at Berkeley]] under [[John L. Kelley]] (Ph.D. on the thesis ''Structure of [[Operator algebra]]s'', 1955),<ref>{{MathGenealogy|31973}}</ref> while working as numerical analyst at [[Lawrence Radiation Laboratory]] (1953–55).  He then joined [[Duke University]] (instructor, 1955–56) and [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (instructor, 1956).  He also worked at [[Lincoln Laboratory]] (1958–66), among others contributing an early study on routing in [[packet switching]] computer networks,<ref>[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/stamp/stamp.jsp?arnumber=1088692 Routing Procedures in Communications Networks] parts I and II, in [[Institute of Radio Engineers|IRE]] PGCS CS-10 No. 4 (1962), pp.
322-329</ref> before becoming associate professor of mathematics at [[Dartmouth College]] (1966) and professor (1969).  He served as a research associate at [[Harvard University]] (1973) and at [[University of California]] (1974 and 1980) while maintaining his professorship at Dartmouth College where he taught until his death in 1996.<ref>[https://math.dartmouth.edu/activities/prosser-lectures/ The Prosser lectures] from [[Dartmouth College]]</ref>

Prosser was also a [[cellist]] and [[sailing]] devotee.  The mathematics department at [[Dartmouth College]] opened the ''Prosser Memorial Lectures'' in 2002.
